title: The Atlantic slave trade: the Middle Passage, its scale and its legacy
examples: How many Africans were taken in the Atlantic slave trade?

explain.say: In 1789 Olaudah Equiano published the story of his life, describing being kidnapped as a child and the horror of a slave ship's hold. His is one voice among about 12.5 million Africans forced onto ships between 1501 and 1866. Please take this history slowly. The board shows where the roughly 10.7 million survivors of the voyage were taken.

draw.text: The Atlantic slave trade: the Middle Passage, its scale and its legacy

explain.say: Look at the map. Most captives came from West and West Central Africa: Senegambia, the Gold Coast in today's Ghana, the Bights of Benin and Biafra in today's Nigeria and Benin, and above all Angola and the Congo region. Some African states and merchants sold captives taken in wars and raids; European traders created the demand. Why does it matter to name both?

See the network. Ships often ran a triangle: goods from Europe to Africa, captives across the Atlantic on the Middle Passage, then sugar back to Europe. But the biggest route was direct, between Angola and Brazil. About 1.8 million people died on the crossing alone. Why was the Middle Passage so deadly?

nodes.label: West Africa
nodes.ask: How many Africans were taken in the Atlantic slave trade?

explain.say: Back to the sizes. Brazil received about 4.9 million people, almost half of all arrivals; North America about 400,000. Enslaved people resisted constantly: revolts on perhaps one voyage in ten, runaway communities like Palmares in Brazil, and the Haitian Revolution from 1791. What does resistance tell you about the people behind the numbers?

Britain banned the trade in 1807, Brazil ended it in 1850 and abolished slavery in 1888. Why did it end? See the debate between Eric Williams and Seymour Drescher. Thank you for learning this with care. Challenge: explore the free Slave Voyages database and read the record of one voyage.

faq.q: How many Africans were taken in the Atlantic slave trade?
faq.a: The Slave Voyages database estimates about 12.5 million people were forced onto ships between 1501 and 1866, and about 10.7 million survived the crossing. Many more died in capture and on the march to the coast.
asks: How big was the transatlantic slave trade?
What were the main routes of the slave trade?

faq.a: The crossing of the Atlantic from Africa to the Americas, the middle leg of the triangular trade. Captives were packed in holds for weeks or months; about 1.8 million people died on these voyages.
asks: Why was the Middle Passage so deadly?

faq.a: Brazil received about 4.9 million, almost half; the British, French, Spanish and Dutch Caribbean and mainland Spanish America took most of the rest; North America received about 400,000.
asks: Why did Brazil receive so many enslaved people?

faq.a: An African-born writer and campaigner, enslaved as a boy, who bought his freedom and in 1789 published his autobiography, a key abolitionist text. Some historians, like Vincent Carretta, question whether he was born in Africa or America.

faq.q: Why did the Atlantic slave trade end?
faq.a: Abolitionist campaigns, including Black writers and petitions, resistance and revolts by enslaved people, especially in Haiti, and changing economics all mattered. Eric Williams stressed economics; Seymour Drescher argued Britain abolished a still-profitable trade.
asks: What was the Eric Williams thesis?

facts: About 12.5 million Africans were embarked on transatlantic slave ships between 1501 and 1866, according to the Slave Voyages database.
Britain abolished its slave trade in 1807.
Brazil abolished slavery in 1888, the last country in the Americas to do so.

quiz.say: About 12.5 million people were embarked and about 10.7 million arrived. About how many died during the voyages?
quiz.why: 12.5 minus 10.7 equals 1.8 million people who died at sea.

wrong.1: That adds the numbers instead of subtracting.
wrong.2: The loss was about nine times larger.

quiz.say: Which region received the most enslaved Africans?
quiz.show: Which region received the most captives?
quiz.why: Brazil received about 4.9 million people, almost half of all arrivals.

wrong.1: North America received about 400,000, under 4 percent.
wrong.2: Very few captives were taken to Europe itself.
